about: About these leads

Leaflegal sends motoring offence enquiries from drivers in England and Wales who want to pay a solicitor to advise or represent them. Each enquiry goes to one firm only. It is never sent to several firms at once and it is never resold after delivery.

People facing a motoring charge are usually very motivated to get help. Their job may depend on driving, they may run a business that needs a vehicle, or they may care for someone who relies on them for lifts. Many have a court date or a deadline on a letter, and they want to know quickly where they stand and what representation would cost.

Every client confirms that they are looking for paid representation rather than free advice. That means your first call can focus on the client's matter and your service, not on whether they are willing to pay.

Many drivers also find it hard to work out which kind of lawyer they need. By asking a few simple questions, our form gets them to a firm that handles motoring work, rather than to a general practice that may pass them on.

Our campaigns run on search, social media and helpful content aimed at drivers who have received a notice of intended prosecution, a court summons, a postal requisition or a letter about their points. Each person answers a short set of questions about the offence, their current points, any court date and where they are. When an enquiry matches your criteria, we check it and send it to you straight away.

about.h3: Why speed matters so much in motoring work

about: Motoring clients are often working to a fixed date. A summons may give a hearing a few weeks away, and a response to a single justice procedure notice has its own deadline. Drivers in that position usually instruct the first firm that explains things clearly and gives them a price. Because each Leaflegal enquiry goes to one firm, you have the chance to be that firm without racing several competitors to the phone.

Leaflegal is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. We do not tell drivers whether they have a defence, whether they are likely to be banned or what to plead. We introduce them to one firm that handles motoring work, and the advice comes from you.
Who enquires

Motoring enquiries come from a broad range of drivers. You choose the offence types you want, so a firm that concentrates on serious charges does not have to take routine speeding matters unless it wants them.

list: Drink driving and drug driving, including failing to provide a specimen
Using a mobile phone while driving
Driving while disqualified or other licence matters

about: Many motoring clients are professional drivers, such as delivery and HGV drivers, sales staff and tradespeople, for whom a ban could mean losing their job. Others are business owners, carers, parents with school runs or people living in rural areas with little public transport. A good number are new drivers worried about the rules that apply in their first two years on the road.

about.h3: Where they are in the process

about: Some drivers enquire as soon as a notice of intended prosecution arrives, before they have responded to it. Others have a court date coming up, have received a single justice procedure notice or have already pleaded and want help with an exceptional hardship argument or mitigation. Each lead says whether there is a court date and what it is, if the client knows it.

Drivers usually want a clear answer to three questions. Can you help, what will it cost and what happens next. Most also want to understand, in general terms, how the process works in the magistrates' court and what kind of outcomes are possible. A firm that explains this calmly, and gives a fixed fee for the work, tends to win their trust.
Lead details
Every motoring lead is the full record of what the driver told us. The questions are short, but they cover what your team needs to triage the matter and quote on the first call.

list: The client's name, a verified UK mobile number and a verified email address
The court date, if the client knows it
The points currently on their licence
Whether the client thinks a ban is likely
Where they are and which court area is likely to be involved
A short description in the client's own words
The source, a timestamp and the consent record

about: Current points help you see quickly whether a matter could lead to a totting up disqualification. Under the totting up rules, a driver who reaches 12 or more points within three years will usually face a disqualification unless the court accepts that exceptional hardship would result. A driver with nine points facing a speeding charge is in a very different position from one with a clean licence, and the lead lets you see that before you call.

Points also matter for newer drivers. A driver who reaches six or more points within two years of passing their test will usually have their licence revoked under the new driver rules. A new driver facing even a modest offence may therefore be very anxious, and the lead helps you spot that.

We ask the client whether they think a ban is likely. This is the client's own view, not an assessment by us, and it may not be accurate. It is still useful, because it tells you what the client is worried about and what they will want to talk about first.

Every client confirms they want paid representation for a matter in England and Wales, and their mobile number and email address are checked. Each one ticks one box to confirm they understand Leaflegal is an introduction service and a separate box to agree to one firm contacting them by phone, email or text. We record the wording and the time and send it with the lead. Leads arrive as soon as they are checked, by email, to a shared inbox or straight into your CRM or case management system.
Working the lead
Motoring enquiries reward firms that are quick, clear and confident about fees. The driver is usually anxious and often has a date in the diary.

about.h3: Call within the hour if you can

about: A driver with a court date coming up will not wait long. Calling soon after the lead arrives, at the time they asked for, shows you take their deadline seriously. Set up alerts so the right fee earner or solicitor advocate sees each lead straight away, including late in the day.

about.h3: Start with the date and the points

about: The lead tells you the offence, the court date and the client's current points. Opening with those shows that you have read their enquiry. It also lets you deal first with anything urgent, such as a response deadline on a notice or a hearing later that week.

Most private motoring clients want a fixed fee for each stage, such as advice and representation at a first hearing, an exceptional hardship argument or a trial. Being clear about what is and is not included, and about any travel or advocacy costs, helps the client say yes on the call.

about.h3: Explain the process in general terms

about: Many drivers have never been to court. A short explanation of how a hearing in the magistrates' court usually runs, how long it might take and what they should bring in general terms can reduce their anxiety a great deal. Keep it general until you have taken instructions and reviewed the evidence.

The client agreed to be contacted after making an enquiry through Leaflegal. Mention that when you call, and cover any referral arrangement in your client care letter as the SRA Code of Conduct requires.

Let us know which leads instruct and which do not. If speeding matters with clean licences rarely convert for you but totting up cases do, we can change your matching to send you more of the work you want.

Follow up matters too. Some drivers want to talk to an employer or family before instructing. A short email after the call setting out your fee and the next step, followed by a second call a day or two later, often helps, especially when a hearing is close.
Compliance
Motoring work is criminal work, and the information drivers share can be sensitive. Leaflegal is set up to support your professional duties.

Leaflegal is an introducer. Under the SRA Code of Conduct, you must make sure clients are told in writing about any financial arrangement with an introducer, and that it does not affect your independence or advice. Our consent wording tells every client we are paid by the firms we introduce them to, and we send that wording with every lead so your client care letter can match it.

Motoring enquiries go to SRA regulated firms and CILEx regulated practices authorised for the work, including rights of audience where you represent clients in court. You remain responsible for your own conflict checks, client identification and fee arrangements, and for your duties to the court.

Motoring enquiries involve information about alleged offences, which UK data protection law treats as criminal offence data. We keep our questions to the minimum needed for first contact and never pass matter details to advertising platforms. Leaflegal, a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, is the controller for data collected on our forms. Once a lead is delivered, you are controller of your copy and handle it under your own privacy notice.

We never tell a driver that a solicitor will keep them on the road or that a charge will be dropped. Our campaigns and form do not promise outcomes, and we expect partner firms to be equally careful in how they describe their service.
Read more about referral rules and introducers.
Pricing

You pay for each motoring lead we deliver, at a price agreed with you before you start. There is no retainer for advertising and no shared or recycled data, so you can measure each lead against the instructions and fees it produces.

Price depends on the offence types and locations you choose. A drink driving or totting up matter where a ban is at stake is usually worth more to a firm than a minor speeding enquiry, and coverage across many court areas produces more matches than a single one. We talk this through on a call and put a proposal together.

The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that, you tell us how many your team can handle and we match to that number. You can set a monthly cap, change it and pause at any time, for example during a run of trials or when an advocate is on leave.

Before your first lead, we agree a written partner agreement covering pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and the rules on invalid leads. If a lead has wrong contact details or falls outside your agreed criteria, tell us within the review period in your agreement and we will deal with it as the agreement says.

Onboarding starts with a 30 minute call with our team. We talk about the motoring work you handle, the courts you cover and your volume, and we show you a sample lead before you commit. You can apply to become a partner firm to book the call.
faqs: The leads
What is a motoring offence lead from Leaflegal?

It is an enquiry from a driver in England and Wales who wants to pay a solicitor to advise or represent them about a motoring offence. They have told us the type of offence, any court date, their current points and whether they think a ban is likely, confirmed their contact details and agreed to be contacted by one firm. We send it to you alone as soon as it is checked.
Are motoring leads exclusive?

Yes. Each enquiry goes to one firm only and is never resold. We do not send the same driver to several firms at once. That matters in motoring work, because drivers with a court date often instruct the first firm that explains things clearly, and an exclusive lead gives you that opportunity without a race against competitors.
Do the clients pay privately?

Yes. Every client confirms they want paid representation rather than free advice. If someone tells us they are only looking for free help, they are pointed elsewhere and do not become a lead. Your first call can therefore focus on the driver's situation, what you can do and what it will cost.
Which offences can I receive?

You can choose from drink and drug driving, speeding, totting up and exceptional hardship, careless and dangerous driving, driving without insurance, failing to identify the driver, mobile phone offences and other licence matters. You can take all of them or only the offence types your team wants, and change the mix later as your practice develops.
Will I know the court date?

Each lead includes the court date if the client knows it. Some drivers enquire before they have a date, for example when a notice of intended prosecution arrives. Others have a hearing coming up soon. Knowing this before you call helps you put the most urgent enquiries in front of a fee earner first.
How reliable is the information about points and bans?

Everything in the lead comes from the client. Drivers usually know roughly how many points they have, but they may be unsure of exact dates or may misunderstand how points are counted. Whether a ban is likely is the client's own view, not our assessment. Treat these answers as a useful starting point and confirm the details when you take instructions.
Do you send leads where the hearing has already happened?

Sometimes a driver contacts us after a first hearing, for example because the case has been adjourned for sentence or they want help with an exceptional hardship argument. The lead and the description in their own words will usually make this clear. If you only want enquiries before a first hearing, tell us and we will set your matching with that in mind.
Do you send enquiries from new drivers?

Yes, if you want them. New drivers are often especially worried, because a driver who reaches six or more points within two years of passing their test will usually have their licence revoked and need to pass again. The lead tells you their current points and the offence, and the description in their own words often mentions when they passed. That helps you prepare for a focused first call.
Volume and areas
How many motoring leads will I receive?

That depends on the offence types and court areas you choose and the enquiries our campaigns are generating at the time. The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that, you set the number your team can handle and we match to it. We will give you an honest view on your call, but we cannot promise a fixed number.
Can I choose the courts or areas I cover?

Yes. You can choose particular towns, counties or regions, or the whole of England and Wales if your advocates travel widely. Because motoring work usually means attending a magistrates' court, many firms prefer areas they can reach easily. Wider coverage usually means more matches but more travel. We will talk through the balance on your call.
Can I set a monthly cap?

Yes. You set the number of leads you want each month, as long as it is at least the minimum of 10. When you reach your cap, we stop matching enquiries to you until the next month. You can change your cap whenever your diary changes, so you never receive more enquiries than you can call quickly.
Can I pause leads?

Yes. If your advocates are fully booked, someone is on leave or you are in a run of trials, tell us and we will pause matching until you are ready again. Pausing does not end your partner agreement, and matching starts again as new enquiries come in once you tell us to restart.
Can leads go to different advocates?

Yes. We can route leads by court area or offence type, so a drink driving enquiry near one office goes to the advocate who covers that court. We can also send everything to a shared intake inbox or your CRM, where you assign leads yourself. We set up whatever suits the way your team works.
Do you send enquiries from Scotland or Northern Ireland?

No. Motoring offence enquiries come from drivers with a matter in England and Wales. Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own court systems and rules, so we do not send those enquiries. Within England and Wales, how many leads you receive depends on the areas and offence types you choose.
Can I receive only enquiries where a ban is likely?

You can tell us which offence types you want, and many firms choose offences where a disqualification is commonly at stake, such as drink driving or totting up. We can also take account of current points when matching. Because whether a ban is likely is the client's own view, we cannot filter perfectly on it, but we can shape your matching around the work you prefer.
Compliance
Do I need to disclose the referral fee?

Yes. Under the SRA Code of Conduct, you must make sure clients are told in writing about any financial arrangement with an introducer, and that it does not affect your independence or advice. Our consent wording tells every client that we are paid by the firms we introduce them to, and we send that wording with each lead so your client care letter can match it.
Does Leaflegal give advice to drivers?

No. Leaflegal is an introduction service, not a law firm. We do not tell drivers whether they have a defence, how to plead or whether they are likely to be banned. We make this clear to every client before they submit. All advice and representation comes from your firm once you are in contact.
How is criminal offence data handled?

Information about alleged offences is treated as criminal offence data under UK data protection law. We keep questions to the minimum needed for first contact and never share matter details with advertising platforms. Leaflegal, a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, is the controller for data collected on our forms. Once a lead is delivered, you are controller of your copy.
How is client consent recorded?

Each client ticks one box confirming they have read our terms and privacy policy and understand that Leaflegal is an introduction service, and a second box agreeing to their details being shared with one firm that may contact them by phone, email or text. We record the exact wording and the time, and the record arrives with the lead.
Who can receive motoring leads?

SRA regulated firms and CILEx regulated practices authorised for the work, including rights of audience where you represent clients in court. You remain responsible for your own regulatory obligations, conflict checks and duties to the court. You must tell us if your authorisation changes, so we can update or pause your matching.
Can we promise clients a result?

How you describe your service is a matter for your firm and your regulator, but outcomes in motoring cases depend on the evidence and the court. Leaflegal never promises drivers a result in our campaigns or on our form, and we expect partner firms to be equally careful, especially with clients who are anxious about losing their licence.
Pricing and terms
How much does a motoring lead cost?

There is no published price list. You pay per lead at a price agreed with you before you start, based on the offence types and areas you choose and the volume you want. We put a proposal together after your onboarding call, so you know the cost of every lead before the first one is delivered.
Is there a written agreement?

Yes. Your partner agreement covers pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and the rules on invalid leads, and it is in place before your first lead. Both sides know from the start what is charged, how leads are counted and how any problem with a lead is handled. We go through it with you and answer any questions before you sign.
What counts as an invalid lead?

Your partner agreement sets this out. It usually covers things like wrong contact details or an enquiry outside your agreed criteria. If you think a lead is invalid, tell us within the review period in your agreement and we will deal with it as the agreement says. A driver deciding not to instruct does not by itself make a lead invalid.
What if the driver has already instructed someone else?

A lead is an introduction rather than a guaranteed instruction, and drivers are free to choose any firm. Calling quickly, giving a clear fixed fee and explaining the next steps are the best ways to win the instruction. If you find a lead is genuinely outside your criteria, raise it within your review period.
Getting started
How do I become a partner firm?

Apply to become a partner firm and book a 30 minute call with our team. We go through the motoring work you handle, the courts you cover, your advocates and your volume. Then we agree your criteria and price, show you a sample lead and put your partner agreement in place before any leads are sent.
Can I see a sample motoring lead?

Yes. On your call we show you a sample motoring lead with every field, the format it arrives in and the consent record. You can see how the offence, court date, points and the client's view on a ban are presented, so you know exactly what your team would receive before you decide.
Is there a portal or login?

No. There is no platform to learn. Leads arrive by email, to a shared intake inbox, or straight into your CRM or case management system using a lead email address or a webhook. Your team works them in the systems they already use, which suits busy advocates who are often out at court.
What should we set up before our first lead?

Decide who calls new leads, especially while advocates are in court. Send leads to a shared inbox or CRM so someone can always pick them up. Prepare a simple fixed fee summary for the main offence types and check that your client care letter covers the referral arrangement as the SRA Code requires.
Can we change our matching later?

Yes. Your criteria are not fixed. If you add an advocate in a new court area, decide you want more drink driving and fewer speeding matters, or want to stop a particular offence type, tell us and we update your matching. Feedback on which leads instruct and which do not helps us send you more of the work that suits your team.
